record.original_question: Let G be a graph homeomorphic to a Moore graph of diameter d and degree k >= 3, with the Moore graph distinct from K_n for n >= 5. If each path of G composed of d successive segments is a geodesic, each cycle of G containing 2d + 1 segments has odd length, and all cycles of G containing 2d + 2 segments have equal length, are these three conditions not only sufficient but also necessary for G to be geodetic?

evidence.quote: More generally, the following three conditions are sufficient for a homeomorphic graph G to any Moore graph of diameter d (k  3) distinct from Kn, n  5, to be geodetic:
(1) Each path of G composed of d successive segments, one followed by the other, is a geodesic in G.
(2) Each cycle of G containing 2d + 1 segments has odd length.
(3) All cycles of G containing 2d + 2 segments have equal length.
It is conjectured that the three conditions of each of the two previous statements are not only sufficient, but also necessary [6].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a Moore graph of diameter $d \geq 1$ and degree $k \geq 3$, that is, a $k$-regular graph of diameter $d$ and girth $2d+1$. Assume $H$ is not the complete graph $K_n$ for any $n \geq 5$.

A graph $G$ is said to be homeomorphic to $H$ if $G$ can be obtained from $H$ by subdividing edges (inserting finitely many vertices of degree $2$ into edges). The maximal paths in $G$ whose internal vertices all have degree $2$ and whose endpoints are vertices of degree $\neq 2$ are called the segments of $G$; thus the segments of $G$ correspond to the edges of $H$.

A graph $G$ is geodetic if every pair of vertices is joined by a unique shortest path.

Consider the following three conditions on a graph $G$ homeomorphic to $H$:
(1) Every path of $G$ consisting of $d$ consecutive segments is a geodesic in $G$.
(2) Every cycle of $G$ consisting of $2d+1$ segments has odd length.
(3) All cycles of $G$ consisting of $2d+2$ segments have the same length.

It is known that conditions (1), (2), (3) together are sufficient for $G$ to be geodetic. Determine whether these three conditions are also necessary: that is, must every geodetic graph $G$ homeomorphic to such a Moore graph $H$ satisfy (1), (2), and (3)?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface related work on enumerating geodetic graphs homeomorphic to a given geodetic graph (including Moore graphs such as the Petersen graph), where analogous three-condition characterizations are stated as sufficient. No source clearly establishes or refutes the necessity of conditions (1)–(3) in the stated generality, so the current status appears unresolved from available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Geodetic Graphs Homeomorphic to a Given Geodetic Graph
status_evidence.snippet: Systematic approach to generating geodetic graphs homeomorphic to a given geodetic graph; states sufficient conditions for Moore-graph homeomorphs.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient conditions analogous to (1)-(3) appear in the literature; necessity in full generality is not asserted.

status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on geodetic graphs and unique-geodesic properties.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on geodetic graph characterizations; no resolution of the stated necessity question identified.
